title: A2-02 · The perfect: complete conjugation · first year budget

blocks.text: A2-02 · The perfect: complete conjugation · budget of
first year
Lesson overview

In A1-18 you learned the perfect to the singular, with ...noi and theirs, and some perfect irregular to memorize. In this unit complete the picture: all thirteen people, the three vowels of the base and, above all, the rule of the two bases that explains why ⁧قَالَ⁩ becomes ⁧قُلْتُ⁩ and ⁧مَشَى⁩ becomes ⁧مَشَيْتُ⁩ . By that rule, the verbs \"irregularÂ" stop being. The second week closes the first year with a budget for skill and plan of the year 2.

rows: A2 · Module A2.1 The verbal system
12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 51–52 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-02), voice synthesis script, progress log (Excel file), tutor session in the second week
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. to combine a regular verb to the perfect in all persons, including women and duals;
2. explain the rule of the two bases and apply it to concave verbs ( ⁧قَالَ⁩ , ⁧بَاعَ⁩ , ⁧نَامَ⁩ ), defects ( ⁧مَشَى⁩ , ⁧دَعَا⁩ , ⁧نَسِيَ⁩ ) and
verbs ⁧جَاءَ⁩ , ⁧رَأَى⁩ , ⁧رَدَّ⁩ ;
3. combine verbs with hamza ( ⁧أَخَذَ⁩ , ⁧سَأَلَ⁩ , ⁧قَرَأَ⁩ , ⁧بَدَأَ⁩ ) and those beginning with ⁧و⁩ ( ⁧وَصَلَ⁩ , ⁧وَضَعَ⁩ );
4. grant the verb with singular, dual and plural subjects, before and after the verb;
5. recognize and use ⁧قَدْ⁩ and ⁧لَقَدْ⁩ with the perfect, as in the news;
6. tell a year or a trip to 90 words and understanding a story at moderate speed;
7. make the first year budget with measured data, skills for skill.
Two-week plan.

2. The perfect in all people
The perfect has only suffixes. Here is the complete conjugation of ⁧دَرَسَ⁩ Studying. The bold lines you already know actively; The others now become active too.
They (f.) ⁧دَرَسْنَهُنَّ⁩ darasna ⁧ـْنَ⁩ -na

Two suffix families. Look at the suffix column: some start with a consonant (-you, -ta, -ti, -ti). tumā, -nā, -tum, -tunna, -na), others with a vowel (-a, -at, -ā, -atā, -ū). In front of the first the base ends with a sukūn (daras-tu); in front of the seconds the base ends with a vowel (darasa, darasat). This difference, which in regular verbs seems a detail, is the key to all weak verbs: keep it in mind for sections 5–7. Tricks to distinguish shapes.
• -na -nā: ⁧دَرَسْنَ⁩ Darasna ... ⁧دَرَسْنَا⁩ darasnā "We" is the name of the company. Without vowels they are only distinguished by the final aliif.

3. The vowel of the base and the verbs of the first year
The basis of the perfect has vowel a, i or, more rarely, u on the second consonant. It is not derived from the meaning: one learns with the verb, together with the vowel of the imperfect.
faʿula – yafʿulu ⁧يَكْبُرُكَبُرَ⁩ (states and quality: ... become big, grow ...)

The rule of A1-18 remains valid: if the perfect has the i, the imperfect has almost always the a. Verbs in faʿula almost always indicate a quality that is acquired ( ⁧كَبُرَ⁩ "Become big" ⁧صَعُبَ⁩ "To become difficult"): they are few and for now you just recognize them. In the dictionary (A2-01Section 7) the vowel of the imperfect is indicated next to the perfect: ⁧كتب⁩ u.a. means ⁧كَتَبَ⁩
4. Verbs with hamza and verbs beginning with ⁧و⁩
With hamza. The hamza is a consonant like the others: the verb is regular. It only changes the support of the hamza, according to the vowels nearby.

In ⁧قَرَؤُوا⁩ the hamza leans on ⁧و⁩ because it is followed by ū. You'll also find the handwriting ⁧قَرَأُوا⁩ : is widespread and accepted. The complete rules of the hamza are in A2-16. With ⁧و⁩ Initial. The perfect are completely regular: ⁧وَصَلْتُ⁩ , ⁧وَصَلَتْ⁩ , ⁧وَصَلُوا⁩ ; ⁧وَضَعْتُ⁩ , ⁧وَضَعُوا⁩ ; ⁧وَقَعَ⁩ , ⁧وَقَعَتْ⁩ . The ⁧و⁩ disappears only to the imperfect ( ⁧يَصِلُ⁩ , ⁧يَضَعُ⁩ : A2-03).
5. Concave verbs: the rule of the two bases
In the verbs "concave" the second consonant of the root is ⁧و⁩ or ⁧ي⁩ : ⁧ق و ل⁩ , ⁧ب ي ع⁩ , ⁧ن و م⁩ . The perfect have two basics:
• in front of the suffixes beginning with a vowel (he, she, the duals of third person, their male): base
long with ā : ⁧قَالَ⁩ , ⁧قَالَتْ⁩ , ⁧قَالَا⁩ , ⁧قَالُوا⁩ ;
• in front of the suffixes that begin with a consonant (all other people): short base, with u or with i:
Why? An Arabic syllable cannot have a long vowel followed by two consonants (*qāltu): the vowel shortens. What short vowel? Look at the imperfect:
with ā: ⁧يَنَامُ⁩ , ⁧يَخَافُ⁩ i ⁧خِفْتُ⁩ , ⁧نِمْتُ⁩
Conjugation complete of ⁧قَالَ⁩ and ⁧بَاعَ⁩ :
They (f.) ⁧قُلْنَ⁩ qualna ⁧بِعْنَ⁩ biʿna
Attention to their (f.) (s.a.) The suffix -na begins with a consonant: then short base, ⁧قُلْنَ⁩ qulna, non *qālna.

us ⁧مَشَيْنَا⁩ mašaynā ⁧دَعَوْنَا⁩ daʿawnā ⁧نَسِينَا⁩ nasīnā

blocks.text: The verb with the subtext brings the subject into the suffix: ⁧دَرَسْنَ⁩ They have studied, ⁧عَادَا⁩ The two of them have returned. In the news the order verb + subject is the norm: the verb remains singular even with plural or dual subjects. In a title without vowels like ⁧وصل الوزيران⁩ the singular verb must not deceive you: the subject is dual,             the two ministers have arrived.
9. ⁧قَدْ⁩ and ⁧لَقَدْ⁩
⁧قَدْ⁩ + Perfect underlines that the action is accomplished: "already," "effectively" often without translation.
• ⁧قَدْ وَصَلَ الوَفْدُ.⁩ The delegation is (already) here.
• ⁧وَقَدْ قَالَ الوَزِيرُ إِنَّ⁩ ... and the minister said that...

⁧لَقَدْ⁩ ( ⁧لَـ⁩ + ⁧قَدْ⁩ ) is more emphatic, typical of formal speech and speeches: ⁧لَقَدْ نَجَحْتَ⁩ ! You really did it!In front of a word with the alif waṣla, ⁧قَدْ⁩ Takes one of the support: ⁧وَقَدِ اجْتَمَعَ الوَزِيرُ⁩ wa-qadi ǧtamaʿa. Denial is done on the verb, without ⁧قَدْ⁩ : ⁧مَا وَصَلَ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يَصِلْ⁩ ( A2-05). To be recognized. ⁧قَدْ⁩ + imperfect has a different value: it may be that, sometimes ( ⁧قَدْ يَتَأَخَّرُ القِطَارُ⁩ The train may be delayed. You'll see it in A2-03.
10. First year budget (week) 52)

The first year ends with a cumulative evaluation, not a new test. Collect data from the log and examination A1 and fill out the table with the tutor. You don't need a perfect result: you need an honest profile, skill skills (Plan, section) 1: () Separate profiles.

How to read the budget. Skills under reference receive more time in the year 2: for reading, 10 minutes per day of reading aloud with a stopwatch; for listening, one script per day heard twice before reading; for the oral, a second weekly session with the tutor. If constancy is below the80%, the problem is not Arabic but the calendar: it goes to the light pace for the module A2.1 instead of accumulating delay (Plan, section 5). The Plan of the Year 2 is written in three lines in the register: rhythm chosen (light, standard, intensive), number of sessions with the tutor per week, skills to be recovered. At the end of A2 the Plan recommends an external feedback: the CIMA level A2 (Plan, section 6.4). If you plan to support it, it already marks the period in the calendar and checks dates and locations on the official website when the time comes.
11. Pronunciation

-ū or -aw? ⁧دَفَعُوا⁩ dafaʿū They have paid for this, and ⁧دَعَوْا⁩ daʿaw They invited several people: ū long versus diphthong aw (as in auto.) In the B script, you feel them alternating. Short base and long base. Hold on to the ā of qāla, zāra, bāʿa and short the vowel of qultu, zurtu, biʿtu: “qooltu” is a common mistake. In the short base the final consonant closes immediately on the suffix: qul-tu, biʿ-tu, nim-tu. The hamza in front of the suffix. In ⁧جِئْتُ⁩ ǧiʾtu and ⁧قَرَأْتُ⁩ qaraʾtu the hamza is a real throat closure before t: do not jump it (notǧitu"N', not "N', "N', "N', "N', "N', "N', "N', "N', "N', "N', "N', "N', "N', "N', "N', "N', "N', "N', "N', "N'. -tum/-tunna. In -tunna the n is double: darastun-na.

Reading 1 · A message to Laylā
⁧عَزِيزَتِي لَيْلَى،⁩
⁧مَرْحَبًا! كَيْفَ حَالُكِ؟ لَقَدِ انْتَهَتِ السَّنَةُ الأُولَى فِي دَرْسِ العَرَبِيَّةِ، وَنَجَحْتُ فِي الاِمْتِحَانِ! قَضَيْنَا سَنَةً جَمِيلَةً:⁩
⁧فِي البِدَايَةِ دَرَسْنَا الحُرُوفَ، ثُمَّ قَرَأْنَا نُصُوصًا قَصِيرَةً، وَفِي النِّهَايَةِ كَتَبْنَا رَسَائِلَ مِثْلَ هٰذِهِ الرِّسَالَةِ.⁩
⁧كَانَ فِي الصَّفِّ عَشَرَةُ طُلَّابٍ: نَجَحَ ثَمَانِيَةٌ، وَتَرَكَ اثْنَانِ الدِّرَاسَةَ بَعْدَ شَهْرَيْنِ. يُوسُف وَسَمِير أَخَذَا نَتَائِجَ⁩

⁧مُمْتَازَةً، وَالطَّالِبَاتُ الثَّلَاثُ مَا تَرَكْنَ دَرْسًا وَاحِدًا. أَمَّا أَنَا فَنَسِيتُ كَلِمَاتٍ كَثِيرَةً، لٰكِنِّي وَجَدْتُهَا فِي أَنْكِي! فِي الأُسْبُوعِ المَاضِي دَعَتْنَا سَلْمَى إِلَى بَيْتِهَا. جِئْنَا كُلُّنَا، وَأَكَلْنَا طَعَامًا مِصْرِيًّا، وَتَكَلَّمْنَا بِالعَرَبِيَّةِ فَقَطْ. مَشَيْتُ⁩
⁧إِلَى البَيْتِ بَعْدَ مُنْتَصَفِ اللَّيْلِ، سَعِيدًا جِدًّا.⁩
⁧وَأَنْتِ؟ هَلْ رَجَعْتِ مِنْ دِمَشْقَ؟ مَاذَا رَأَيْتِ هُنَاكَ؟⁩
⁧لُوكَامَعَ السَّلَامَةِ،⁩
